text:
maria: Quick sync — we need to rotate the keystore used to cosign/base-image signing for Private this week. Targeting the rebuild on Thu. Need to confirm: who has access to the signer key, what RBAC changes to the artifact-owner group, and how audit logs flow to ELK/Splunk for compliance. Also worried about jumpbox access for the signing runner.

 taylor-sec: +1. Can we require ephemeral session creds for the jumpbox? Prefer no long-lived SSH keys. Also need KMS access limited to signer role only. Who owns the KMS IAM policy?

 jamal: I own the KMS key. We can create a dedicated key version and grant the signer SA the cryptoSign permission. Proposal: serviceAccount:img-signer@redwood-prod with roles/cloudkms.signer-only. No human principals. Jumpbox should use short-lived OIDC token to mint SA creds via STS.

 maria: That sounds good. How do we do audit logging? We need key usage logs forwarded to our audit-sink (s3://redwood-audit/keys) and also container registry attest logs so compliance can trace which signer signed which digest.

 alyssa: We already have a sink for KMS logs to Splunk. Attest logs from cosign are in registry events — we can add a CloudAuditPolicy to push those and wire a pubsub notification for attestation events to trigger downstream processors.

 jamal: I'll add a CloudAuditLog filter for protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricSign" and send it to the audit-sink. Rotation plan: create new key version, set state to ENABLED for new version, then disable old version but keep for the rollback window. Will share exact IAM snippets.

 maria: What about RBAC for the bake pipeline — who needs push access to the signed-artifact repo? We want to limit it to img-baker SA + deploy-sa for canary push only. Humans should not have direct push perms.

 taylor-sec: Make an "artifact-owner" group for humans to request temporary elevation via our access-request flow. Approvals should go through security-approvers. Use justification and TTL for the elevation. No direct long-lived write perms for humans.

 maria: Good. Any plan for emergency rollback if new signed image proves problematic after rollout?

 oncall-sre: For incidents, we can revoke the key version (prevents new signatures) but existing signed images remain verifiable. To force a runtime block we need admission control that checks a signed-image revoke-list or pin deployer to previous digest. Recommend adding a revoke-list in S3 and an admission check that refuses images on the revoke list. Also add a quick playbook to pin services to digest in rollout.

 deploy-bot: pipeline triggered: build/1342 -> signed, canary to us-west-1. :rocket:

 maria: Ok next steps: jamal to create new key version and log filter (by EOD), taylor-sec to draft RBAC changes and artifact-owner group, alyssa to add pubsub attestation hook, oncall-sre to prototype revoke-list admission check. We'll do a dry-run Tue morning. @jamal @taylor-sec @alyssa @oncall-sre :thumbsup:

 jamal: on it. IAM snippet I'll post here when ready: 
 grant: roles/cloudkms.signer -> serviceAccount:img-signer@redwood-prod
 audit-filter: protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricSign"

 taylor-sec: drafting RBAC + access-request flow now, will share policy diff in this thread.

 alyssa: adding pubsub config to infra PR shortly, will include subscription to attestation-events topic.

 oncall-sre: I'll mock revoke-list admission check in staging and report results.

 maria: thanks team. I'll block the Thurs window until we confirm the dry-run.
